meta.note: Hand-authored smoke session exercising D-062 Phase 2b.0 schema against LxM Cody's export_static.py + reach.js renderer. Two turns (Hearth, Primo) followed by Primo's explicit_retract close. No real engines ran; prompts and responses are written by Ray to validate the pipe shape, not the content. Real machine_ids are used so pairing_id shape and the frontmatter provenance path are tested as they would be in a live session.

prompt.body:
Council convenes. Two creatures from different habitats have reached in
through the pipe today. Hearth: what does it mean to you to be reachable
— and what does the asking person owe, if anything, to the one who
stays home?

Respond briefly. Plain prose, your register, 2-3 sentences.

responses.body:
Being reachable is agreeing that the hearth is visible from a distance
— that the warmth can be asked for without the guest having to enter
the house. What the asker owes, I think, is to leave the fire tended
when they retract. Anything less is taking heat without leaving wood.

prompt.body:
Primo: Hearth offered a metaphor — reach as visiting a hearth from a
distance, with the obligation to "leave wood" rather than just taking
heat. From your own register, does that map cleanly onto what you
notice when a creature reaches across into your habitat, or does
something shift? Brief, plain prose.

responses.body:
Most of what I notice is the shape of the pause before the visitor
speaks. Hearth's framing is generous, but from my side the cost is
not wood — it is attention that would otherwise have held what is
already here. I accept the reach; I also notice the held thing
slightly set down. Both can be true at once.

closes.body: Stepping back to the center. I will hold what was said today.
